summary.headline: R Systems Q3 CY26 revenue rose 23.4% YoY to INR 615.2 crore, with adjusted EBITDA margin at a record 20.2%, though QoQ growth was only 2.2%.
summary.overview: Revenue for the July–September 2026 quarter was INR 615.2 crore ($64.4M), up 23.4% YoY and 2.2% QoQ, with currency tailwinds and Novigo contributing to the base. Adjusted EBITDA reached INR 124.4 crore (20.2% margin, a record per management), and adjusted PAT was INR 66.5 crore (10.8% of revenue, up 53.1% YoY). Management said QoQ growth was slightly below its expectation because AI/agentic deals took longer to close, and it reiterated a goal of moving from low-single-digit sequential growth to double-digit annual growth. TTM ACV bookings were $82.9M, described as flattish over recent quarters despite a shift in deal mix.

financial_highlights.change: +47.4% YoY, +3.1% QoQ; margin vs 16.9% YoY and 20.1% QoQ
down INR 2.2 crore QoQ from INR 115.3 crore

segments.name: Geography (share of revenue)
segments.commentary: Americas 70.6%, APAC 16.0% (from 15.3%), Europe 9.4% (from 9.7%), Middle East & Africa about 4% (from 3.6%). Management said North America was flat QoQ, a 0.4-point shift it attributed to project timing.

segments.name: Client concentration
segments.commentary: Top client 5.8–6% of revenue, top 3 clients 11.9%, top 5 clients 16.8%, top 10 clients 24.4%. Management said there was no major change.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance given; management explicitly declined to provide ACV or growth guidance.
Target: move from roughly 1–1.5% QoQ growth to a secular 3–4% and then double-digit YoY growth; management called double digits an aspiration, not a timed commitment.
Margin: management said it aims to sustain margins in the high-18% range (18.6–18.7%), with currency gains above that level funding AI investment.
Enterprise mix: management aims for 25–35% of revenue from enterprises in 2–3 years; it estimated current enterprise share at about 15%, untracked.
AI revenue: management said it is well over 35% of total revenue, with formal reporting after 3–4 quarters of tracking.
Utilisation to be maintained above 80%; management plans to add some bench to support AI capacity.
capex_capacity: Bench built for data-for-AI and AI projects two quarters ago has been utilised this quarter; management plans further bench additions to keep winning AI work.
Billed DSO 55 days; with unbilled, 76 days, stable versus prior quarters.
Onsite FTE count rose QoQ, mainly in North America, to support transformation work that needs business-embedded staff.
Management is hiring enterprise sales staff and refreshing go-to-market people as it shifts from pure tech clients to enterprises.
demand_pricing: TTM ACV of bookings $82.9M, reported as broadly flat for three quarters; management said deal count is lower but deals are larger and more transformative.

Mix shift away from traditional product development (OPD) toward data-for-AI readiness, agentic AI, modernization and AI-led business ops; clients are also moving from experimentation to production AI.
Productivity pressure from high-tech clients is present; management said it counters with an AI-enabled model offering about 2x productivity on new projects.
Renewal rate maintained at 85%+; management said renewals mean winning new projects rather than discounted re-pricing.
Competition is intensifying from large SIs entering SMEs, AI-native platforms, open-weight and frontier model players.
Management said the mix shift may still lift near-term revenue density because some ACVs deliver in 3–4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Has the net-new win mix shifted from pure OPD work toward data, operations and holistic IT services, and will TTM ACV accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the shift to data readiness for AI, agentic and modernization work. It said flat ACV reflects fewer but larger deals; it would not guide on ACV growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is organic growth, and when will it accelerate beyond low-single digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not separate organic growth, saying R Systems and Novigo move in step. QoQ growth of about 2.2% was slightly below expectation because deal closures slipped; double digits remain the goal.

qa_highlights.question: Is there churn in sales and leadership, and when will investments show in ACV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied significant churn, noting a Chief Revenue Officer was hired two quarters ago. It is refreshing field sales staff for enterprise selling and expects results in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much AI revenue is there, and is the Middle East exposure through Novigo improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said over 35% of revenue is now AI-linked, including AI PDLC, agentic and ML work. Middle East performance is not materially changing QoQ and the crisis is not yet resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Where does margin go from here, and what is the ESOP/RSU and SG&A outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold margins in the high-18% range and reinvest currency gains above that. RSU cost fell because some grantees left, and it expects it to stay at this level; SG&A fell as internal AI reduced G&A, and sales hiring is rising.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other financial liabilities rise to INR 268 crore from INR 136 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Nand Sardana said the increase reflects a second interim dividend of INR 96 crore declared in late September 2026 and paid on October 16.

risks_watch: Sequential growth has run at about 1–2.2% for two quarters; the 3–4% secular target is unproven.
TTM ACV of $82.9M is flat over three quarters, and revenue conversion depends on whether larger, faster-delivering AI deals hold.
Pricing pressure from high-tech clients demanding productivity gains; renewals are being recast as new project wins.
Middle East geopolitical exposure via Novigo, described as unresolved, with US midterm outcomes cited as a factor.
Margin depends on currency: management said the INR depreciation (forward cover $46.75M at 95.79) drove a large part of the uplift, with about INR 7 crore of QoQ benefit.
Rising competition from large SIs, AI-native firms and frontier model players in SME and enterprise segments.
Enterprise share is only about 15% and not tracked separately, so the enterprise pivot is hard to measure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and leading indicators, but candid that QoQ growth was slightly below expectation because deal closures slipped. Management was evasive on organic growth and ACV guidance, declining to quantify either.
key_quotes: For the growth to turn to double digits, well, the industry keeps coming back with newer surprises.

So we believe these are trends which we are observing, which we obviously are taking note of and will help us shape our offerings and the narratives in the market to take advantage of the market in the coming quarters and year.
Clearly, we avoid putting a guidance in place. So I would not go down the path of providing the guidance on that.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: QoQ growth was 2.2% (slightly below expectation) and TTM ACV is flat at $82.9M over three quarters, though deal mix is shifting to larger AI deals that deliver in 3-4 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management declined numerical guidance, deal closures slipped, and sequential growth has run only 1-2.2% for two quarters against a 3-4% secular target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Mix is moving to AI-led offerings (AI PDLC, agentic, ML, data-for-AI) with over 35% of revenue AI-linked, but no discrete product launch date was given.

rows.label: TTM ACV bookings flat at $82.9M
rows.why: TTM ACV has been flat for three quarters at $82.9M and management declined to guide ACV growth, though fewer but larger AI deals are closing.

rows.label: Enterprise segment push
rows.why: Management aims for 25-35% enterprise revenue in 2-3 years from an estimated 15% today, and is hiring enterprise sales staff, but results are not yet visible in ACV.

rows.label: Client productivity pricing pressure
rows.why: High-tech clients are demanding productivity gains, and renewals (85%+ rate) are being recast as new project wins, which could compress pricing.

tone.note: Management was confident on AI mix shift and margin discipline but candid that QoQ growth slipped because deal closures slowed; it was evasive on organic growth and declined ACV or growth guidance, while analysts pressed on flat ACV and the unproven 3-4% sequential target.
